conventions.convention: Blocks partition labels 1 through d into nonempty sets; label j denotes standard coordinate j−1. Block gradient entries are ordered increasingly.
L_i > 0 bounds variation of the block gradient when only that block changes; model majorizers satisfy M_i ≥ L_i.

Finite-horizon expectations are finite weighted sums over independent block-index histories. Rate statements require the claimed updates to execute without early stopping; the composite-curvature theorem explicitly requires accepted certificates at every history, without conditioning on success.
Closed convex penalties use closed epigraphs; finite separable sums are proved closed by neighborhood arguments rather than an unstated sequential-closure equivalence.
Certified inexact updates require a valid nonnegative model-value gap bounded by the prescribed tolerance; an unavailable or invalid certificate returns inner-solve-failure.
The sharper factor 1−μ/(nL_max) assumes strong convexity of f itself. Strong convexity of F alone gives the separately proved factor 1−μ/[n(L_max+μ)], without requiring μ ≤ L_max.
Cyclic minimization permits arbitrary minimizing selections, but the convergence theorem assumes unique continuous block-minimizer maps, a convex separable composite, and a compact initial sublevel.
The Lasso objective is n⁻¹‖y−Xθ‖²+2τ‖θ‖₁ with τ > 0. Nonzero-column updates threshold at nτ; zero columns have the separate unique update zero.

load_bearing.statement: Let f: R^d → R be continuously differentiable, let B_i be one block of a finite coordinate partition, and let U_i be its coordinate insertion map. Suppose L_i > 0 satisfies ‖∇_i f(x+U_i h)−∇_i f(x)‖₂ ≤ L_i‖h‖₂ for every x,h. Then f(x+U_i h) ≤ f(x)+⟨∇_i f(x),h⟩+(L_i/2)‖h‖₂².

For the model and inputs of alg-randomized-coordinate-proximal-descent, every selected exact block subproblem has a unique minimizer. If the update is exact, the objective does not increase. If its accepted inner point has certified model gap at most ε_k, then the new objective is at most the old objective plus ε_k.

Let n ≥ 1 be finite, let d_i ≥ 1, and let each g_i: R^{d_i} → (−∞,+∞] be proper, closed, and convex in the epigraph convention. On the product define g(x)=Σ_i g_i(x_i). Then g is proper, closed, and convex.

For differentiable convex f and a proper closed convex separable g=Σ_i g_i with proper closed convex block terms, if F(x)<+∞ and x globally minimizes every block slice of F=f+g, then −∇_i f(x) ∈ ∂g_i(x_{B_i}) for every i, −∇f(x) ∈ ∂g(x), and x is a global minimizer of F.

Fix a block i and define m_i(a)=min_u{f(a,u)+g_i(u)}, where f is finite and continuous and g_i is proper closed convex. Suppose the minimizer map T_i(a) exists, is unique, and is continuous on the parameter set in question. Then m_i is continuous there.
Let a > 0, b ∈ R, and τ > 0. The scalar convex function q(u)=(a/2)u²−bu+τ|u| has the unique global minimizer u*=S_τ(b)/a. At b=τ and b=−τ, the unique minimizer is 0.

For the stated positive-penalty Lasso objective, fixing the other coefficients and r_j=y−Σ_{ℓ≠j}X_ℓθ_ℓ, a nonzero column has unique minimizing coordinate S_{nτ}(X_j^T r_j)/‖X_j‖₂². A zero column has unique minimizing coordinate zero.
